remarks: Imagine starting your day surrounded by tall pines, watching golfers play through the fairway below as the mountain wakes up. Furnishing and brand new 4 person golf cart included with purchase.

A few minutes from the village, and a short drive to Big Sur, Paso Robles wine country, many beaches to meet your needs, and our big city of San Luis Obispo!!  Call your realtor today for a private showing.

remarks: Moments from Abbot Kinney and the beach, yet completely removed once the gates close, 554 Westminster is a home for thinkers, creators and innovators. It represents tranquility, wellness, nature and exceptional design in balance. There is truly nothing else like it. Hidden behind towering bamboo and mature hedges, the property exists as its own private world in the heart of Venice. It is a refuge from the energy outside; a place to slow down, think clearly, create, gather and reset. Green, light, wood and water form the language of the home, bringing nature into view from nearly every window. Originally conceived by notable Los Angeles architect Charles Ward, whose work is distinguished by clean lines, industrial structure and organic warmth, the residence was later reimagined by David Hertz, FAIA, the Venice-rooted pioneer of sustainable and regenerative design. Their combined vision gives the home a character that feels impossible to reproduce. It is raw yet warm, dramatic yet deeply grounded, equally compelling as an architectural showpiece and a place of complete restoration. Inside, soaring ceilings, exposed wood and steel, polished concrete and custom architectural glass create rooms of remarkable volume and texture. The kitchen anchors the main level with sculptural concrete surfaces, rich wood cabinetry, premium appliances, open shelving and built-in seating designed for both everyday living and entertaining. A bedroom on this level offers flexibility for guests or work. Upstairs, two en-suite bedrooms are joined by an expansive additional living space that overlooks the main floor beneath a series of skylights. A striking bridge of wood and steel leads to the private primary suite, where both the bedroom and bath open to a broad terrace overlooking the garden. At the center of the property's lifestyle is the newly completed, three-level wellness and guest retreat designed by Hertz. The ground floor brings together a sauna, steam room, cold plunge, outdoor shower and kitchen, creating a private environment devoted entirely to health and recovery. Above is an en-suite guest bedroom, while the rooftop becomes an extraordinary open-air entertaining space with a retractable television, fire pit, built-in barbecue and summer kitchen. Between the two structures, the backyard unfolds beneath a canopy of greenery with a swimming pool, spa, fire pit and multiple places to dine, lounge and connect. Tall bamboo and dense hedging provide exceptional privacy, while the interplay of concrete, wood, steel, water and landscape makes the entire property feel alive. Parking for four includes two spaces in the garage and two within the gated driveway. Some homes impress you. Others change the way you feel. 554 Westminster does both.

remarks: Completely reimagined, 3684 Willowcrest Ave is a thoughtful study in restraint, materiality, and the balance between masculine and feminine design. Rather than erase the home's original identity, the redesign celebrates its mid century ranch architecture, preserving its character while elevating every room through custom craftsmanship and carefully considered materials. Set behind ficus hedges, the home feels private from the moment you arrive. A generous front yard leads to the original fluted glass entry, where Concrete Collaborative terrazzo transitions into warm white oak flooring and introduces the material palette carried throughout the home. At the heart of the house is a fully custom white oak kitchen wrapped in Ceppo marble, complete with extensive millwork, a walk in pantry, and dedicated coffee bar. Large bifold doors blur the line between indoors and out, connecting the living spaces to the backyard and outdoor fireplace and allowing the home to live as effortlessly outside as it does within. Every space has its own identity. The powder room pairs Concrete Collaborative honed tile and terrazzo stone top, while both guest baths feature Concrete Collaborative Scala terrazzo. Across three bedrooms and three and a half baths, texture, tone, and natural materials create a home that feels layered rather than overdesigned. The primary suite opens completely to the backyard, while its bath combines white oak mill work, green Italian granite, and a newly installed nostalgic glass block wet room illuminated by a skylight above. Outside, intentional landscaping and architectural lighting create a private retreat with an outdoor fireplace, sunken hot tub, sauna, and generous front and rear yards. Moments from all the shops and restaurants on Ventura Boulevard yet tucked into a quiet residential setting, 3684 Willowcrest is a one of one by design studio, House of Senn. Where the original architecture informed every decision and every detail was considered.

remarks: Le Chateau is one of those special Oakland properties that feels magical from the moment you arrive. Its beautifully landscaped courtyard winds through mature greenery, terracotta-tiled stairs and decorative ironwork, giving the eight-unit community a wonderful old-Hollywood character. 208 Lee Street carries that character inside, with nearly 1,700 square feet spread across three levels. The main floor feels substantial and distinctly home-like, with the living and dining spaces separated from the bedrooms above. In the living room, a beautiful exposed wood-beamed ceiling, brick fireplace and large windows give the room warmth and architectural presence. Hardwood floors continue into the dining room, a space made for lingering over dinner with friends. Just beyond, the kitchen offers abundant cabinetry and stainless appliances, with a powder room conveniently nearby. Upstairs are two bedrooms and a full bath. The primary bedroom is especially spacious, with an adjoining dressing and closet area that includes a built-in desk—a charming and useful little space for getting ready, additional clothing storage or a compact work area. The second bedroom is also nicely proportioned and filled with natural light. Downstairs, the private one-car garage opens directly into a large unfinished bonus area with laundry and generous under-stair storage. It is highly useful as it stands for bikes, projects, gear and everyday overflow, while the size of the room leaves room to imagine something more finished—a media room, lounge, exercise space or other flexible use with thoughtful improvements. A covered patio just outside opens to the surrounding greenery. And Adams Point makes an especially good backdrop. Lake Merritt and Lakeside Park are nearby, along with the restaurants, cafés and shops of Grand Avenue. The Grand Lake Theatre and Saturday farmers market are close at hand, with Uptown and 19th Street BART also within easy reach. There is plenty happening nearby, while Le Chateau itself feels surprisingly tucked away. With its vintage architecture, generous proportions, private garage and stunning grounds, 208 Lee Street offers the ease of condominium ownership in a space that simply feels much more like a home.

remarks: A massive price adjustment makes this iconic estate the most exciting opportunity on the market this year. Hands down, the property is positioned for an immediate sale. Whether you're looking for your forever home or an excellent investment opportunity, an offering of this caliber is a rarity. Available for the first time in over 30 years, this magical residence offers a level of serenity that is next to impossible to find close to town. Sited on nearly two breathtaking acres, there is a deeply moving sense of permanence among the spectacular grounds that is hard to describe. Adorned with a magnificent Heritage Oak and a canopy of stately mature trees, It's the kind of place you'll never want to leave. The notable estate is anchored by a grand stone-and-iron main entrance gate with a sweeping driveway that curves gracefully to a separate exit gate. From its elevated vantage point on an enormous flat knoll, the property delivers long-range views of the Santa Monica Mountains and overlooks state parkland. The exterior amenities cater to a relaxed lifestyle, showcasing a rock-rimmed swimming pool, an abundance of outdoor entertainment spaces, a charming potting house for the avid gardener, and a full-size, lighted tennis court that can easily adapt into two pickleball courts. There is also plenty of room to build an ADU, house a car collection and install a vegetable garden. Inside, the nearly 6,500-square-foot main residence is a masterclass in classic craftsmanship, defined by rich millwork, authentic leaded glass windows, six custom fireplaces, and dual staircases. The interior spaces are grand yet inviting, highlighted by an exquisite formal dining room with a hand-carved wood fireplace and a richly appointed pub room that evokes the sophisticated ambiance of a library bar from another era. A large butler's kitchen sits between the dining room and main kitchen, effortlessly enhancing all manner of entertainment and culinary pursuits.  The massive artist's studio, with voluminous ceiling and separate entrance, provides a versatile space filled with light. The flexible floor plan features dual primary retreats, the largest of which is on the first floor. It comprises two fully appointed bathrooms and an abundance of closet space. A centrally located family room is just off the kitchen as is the delightful sunroom facing the lush backyard pool area. Upstairs, a second primary suite shares the floor with a third en-suite bedroom and an optional fourth bedroom. This secluded haven delivers a rare opportunity to be out of the public eye without sacrificing convenience. Located in the coveted community of Old Agoura, the property is near Cheeseboro Canyon, providing immediate access to over 4,000 acres of hiking, cycling, and equestrian trails. While the property is secluded, it's only minutes from town and about 20 minutes to Malibu beaches. The property is served by the renowned Las Virgenes School District and outstanding private academies. This is one of the most coveted residences to come on the market in decades.

Located at the end of a long private drive within the coveted equestrian enclave of Rancho Cuerno Largo, 3110 Acampo Road is a remarkable ±19-acre estate where California ranch living meets the beauty, equestrian heritage, and relaxed sophistication of the Santa Ynez Valley. Sweeping 360-degree views encompass Ballard Canyon, Grass Mountain, rolling hills, and oak-studded countryside.

Designed to embrace its setting, the approximately 3,254-square-foot custom California ranch home was created by renowned architect Robert Ingle Hoyt and builder Erling Pohls. Centered around a courtyard, the single-level residence opens to expansive outdoor living spaces overlooking the Valley. Vaulted ceilings, an open floor plan, two fireplaces, abundant natural light, and sweeping views create a strong connection to the surrounding landscape.

The main residence offers three bedrooms and three bathrooms, plus a flexible-use room opening to the courtyard that is currently utilized as a bedroom and equally suited as an office, studio, or den. The primary suite and second bedroom feature en-suite baths. Privately positioned in its own wing, the third bedroom offers a separate entrance, living area, and en-suite bath, creating an inviting retreat for guests or extended family. A dedicated workspace and laundry area are conveniently located behind the kitchen.

A circa-late-1800s farmhouse adds historic character with four bedrooms, two baths, and covered porches. Thoughtfully restored over the years, it retains a connection to the property’s agricultural past. Two additional farmworker quarters further support guest, staff, and ranch functions.
Equestrian amenities include a 14-stall stable, large arena, round pen, substantial hay barn with bathroom, cross-fenced turnouts, and ride-out access to equestrian trails. Additional ranch improvements provide space for offices, management, equipment, storage, and operational uses. Two wells support the agricultural and equestrian functions, while AG-1-20 zoning offers flexibility for a range of ranch uses.

Just moments from the village of Los Olivos, the property offers a tranquil setting surrounded by vineyards, working ranches, and open landscapes. Here, equestrian tradition, architectural character, natural beauty, and proximity to wine country converge in a rare Santa Ynez Valley offering.

remarks: One of the most extraordinary residential offerings in Southern California, 380 S. San Rafael Avenue stands as arguably Pasadena's premier estate, an irreplaceable Jacobean Tudor Revival masterpiece set on nearly 5 private, gated acres in the city's most prestigious enclave. Commissioned by the Bernard family and designed by the acclaimed architectural firm Morgan, Walls & Clements, the residence was completed in 1928 and represents an unparalleled combination of architectural significance, scale, privacy, and provenance. Hidden behind gates and enveloped by majestic oaks, manicured gardens, and rolling lawns, the approximately 18,665-square-foot manor commands breathtaking views across the Arroyo Seco, creating the rare feeling of an English country estate in the heart of Pasadena. Its iconic castellated tower, slate rooflines, leaded-glass windows, and exquisitely preserved period detailing showcase a level of craftsmanship and permanence that is virtually impossible to replicate today. Steeped in cultural history, the estate is recognized worldwide as the exterior of Wayne Manor in the original Batman television series and has been featured in numerous acclaimed film and television productions. Yet beyond its celebrated pedigree, the property offers every modern luxury, including a resort-caliber pool, pickleball court, private theater, and exceptional indoor and outdoor spaces designed for both intimate family living and grand-scale entertaining. Originally showcased in Architectural Digest, this singular estate is more than a home; it is one of Pasadena's defining landmarks and an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire what many would consider the finest legacy property in the city.

remarks: Live Where Others Vacation — Without Ever Feeling the Neighbors. Steps from the sand and the soul of Surf City, this 2 bed, 2 bath beach retreat puts you at the center of everything Huntington Beach has to offer — with a layout that feels more like a private beach house than a condo. Here's what most buyers don't expect: this unit shares only one interior wall with another residence — and that wall belongs to a closet. In practice, that means no shared walls with any bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, and very minimal living area. It's the kind of quiet you don't find in most multi-unit buildings, coastal or otherwise. Two of them are yours, deeded to this unit, giving you secure storage for boards, bikes, and all your beach gear, plus parking you don't have to think twice about. The HOA handles landscaping and exterior maintenance, so low-maintenance beach living is genuinely attainable here. Wake up to salt air and ocean breeze. Walk to the pier, Pacific City, and to the energy of Main Street in minutes. Catch the 4th of July Celebration and the Air Show right over the water, or take the short walk to dog-friendly Huntington Dog Beach with your pup. This is the address people dream about — with a layout most of them never knew to ask for.

The kitchen is as much about design as function. A striking aqua Pyrolave lava-stone cooking surface, custom made in France, provides an artful counterpoint to the Caesarstone surfaces. Gaggenau, Thermador, and Bosch appliances—including a gas cooktop, steamer, and deep fryer—complete a kitchen conceived well beyond the ordinary. Beyond the community, the beach is just a short walk away, leading to a quiet stretch of sand that feels remarkably private. Huntington Dog Beach, Pacific City, the Huntington Beach Pier, and downtown are all nearby, creating an unusual balance of privacy, resort-like living, and effortless access to the coast.

Distinctive in its position, its design, and its outlook, this is a Surfcrest residence that stands apart.

remarks: Internationally published and widely recognized for its architectural significance, this exceptional ground-up residence by Woods + Dangaran, completed in 2015, is a masterful expression of California mid-century modernism, where architecture, landscape, and light exist in complete harmony. Hidden behind soaring bamboo hedges in Santa Monica's coveted North of Montana neighborhood, the home reveals itself with quiet confidence, unfolding through a carefully choreographed sequence of spaces that celebrate openness, privacy, and an effortless connection to the outdoors. Every line has been thoughtfully composed and every proportion carefully considered. Expansive walls of glass, warm cedar detailing, polished concrete floors, rich hardwoods, and crisp white planes create a timeless material palette that is both restrained and inviting. Natural light animates the interiors throughout the day, while eleven skylights wash the second floor in soft daylight, enhancing the home's quiet, gallery-like atmosphere. Carefully framed views of sculptural gardens, tranquil courtyards, and open sky dissolve the boundary between indoors and out. Designed as a carefully choreographed sequence of interconnected spaces, the home unfolds from sophisticated entertaining areas to intimate private retreats, with each room revealing a new relationship to the surrounding landscape through landscaped courtyards, garden terraces, and expansive walls of glass. At its center, a serene pool courtyard serves as the home's focal point, enveloped by mature bamboo, architectural succulents, and specimen cacti to create a private, resort-inspired sanctuary where the landscape is every bit as intentional as the architecture itself. The kitchen is a study in understated luxury, appointed with custom Bulthaup cabinetry, a complete suite of Gaggenau appliances including integrated refrigeration, convection oven, a built-in coffee system, a wine refrigerator that holds 41 bottles, and a warming drawer, all complemented by Dornbracht fixtures and thoughtfully curated European finishes. Positioned at the heart of the home, it anchors the surrounding living and entertaining spaces while maintaining the clean restraint that defines the architecture. Beyond the public spaces, the private quarters embrace the same philosophy of quiet luxury. The primary suite serves as a peaceful retreat, where warm wood detailing, soft natural light, and tranquil garden outlooks create an atmosphere of calm. Thoughtfully positioned for privacy, it embodies the home's seamless dialogue between architecture and landscape, offering a sanctuary that feels both intimate and deeply connected to its surroundings. Throughout the home, iconic lighting by Poul Henningsen, Verner Panton, Arne Jacobsen, and Fabricius & Kastholm reinforces the residence's enduring design pedigree, where every material, fixture, and finish has been selected with extraordinary intention. Rarely does a home achieve such a harmonious balance of architectural pedigree, material integrity, and everyday livability. More than a residence, this is a meticulously crafted work of architecture that embodies the enduring principles of California mid-century modernism while offering an exceptional lifestyle in one of Santa Monica's most coveted neighborhoods.

remarks: At the Villages at Rio Del Sol, buyers can explore a community that combines fresh home design with the comfort of a neighborhood already coming to life in the Greater Palm Springs area. Functional living areas, integrated kitchens, and open floor concepts help create spaces that feel connected while spacious, all without sacrificing purpose. remarks: A Rare Mission Hills Opportunity! Why rent when you can own?  Tucked along a quiet, tree-lined street in the heart of Mission Hills, this fully renovated 2-bedroom, 2-bath home is a turnkey entry point into San Diego homeownership, with updated plumbing, electrical, and systems throughout. Previously operated as a short-term rental, this property offers an opportunity for short-term and mid-term investors alike, and RM-2-5 zoning within a Transit Priority Area opens the door to a potential ADU for buyers looking to add rental income or multigenerational living space.  Location is premium here, just minutes from Downtown San Diego, Little Italy, San Diego International Airport and beaches -One of the most convenient and premier locations the city has to offer.  Just a block away, stroll to the intimate India Street enclave, where an evening walk leads past the Shakespeare Pub, a local gelato shop and neighborhood cafes, plus fresh seafood and craft pubs. Meticulously designed and maintained garden retreat, peaceful and made for morning coffee, al fresco dinners and effortless entertaining.  A private driveway and attached garage provide plenty of parking, while a separate shed adds the storage.  A peekaboo ocean and city view Just 3 miles from San Diego International Airport, yet outside the direct flight path, this home offers convenience, a rare combination for first time buyers and investors alike. remarks: Top-floor two-story condominium with 2 bedrooms, 2.5 bathrooms and 1,298 square feet at The Terraces in Dublin. Built in 2007 by Toll Brothers, this residence flips the usual floor plan — living space on the entry level, bedrooms tucked below — so the park and ridgeline views land in the rooms you actually use.  The entry level opens to a great room with a fireplace, hardwood floors and windows on two sides. The kitchen adjoins it with granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, a gas range and a breakfast bar, with a dining area between the two. Glass doors open to a covered balcony set behind a dramatic arched opening. A powder room and a stacked in-unit laundry closet round out this floor.  Downstairs, the primary suite offers its own balcony, a walk-in closet and an en-suite bath with dual vanities, a walk-in shower and a separate water closet. The second bedroom sits opposite a full bath with tub-shower combination — an easy fit for guests, a roommate or a home office. Central air conditioning, forced-air heat, hardwood floors and bedroom carpeting run throughout.  Two side-by-side spaces in the secured underground garage convey with the home, and an elevator serves the building from the garage up. This building has resort-style amenities — swimming pool, spa, fitness center, clubhouse, media room and a rec room with fireplace — along with exterior maintenance, trash removal, hazard insurance and gated security.  The Terraces sits in the middle of Dublin Ranch. Bray Commons park is a short walk, Emerald High School is minutes away, and Kaiser Permanente Dublin plus neighborhood shopping and dining are a quick drive. Commuters get fast access to I-580, I-680 and the Dublin/Pleasanton BART station.

remarks: Steeped in Los Angeles history and layered with opportunity, this remarkable multi-structure property offers far more than square footage alone. Long associated with the historic Phyllis Wheatley Home, the residence carries a meaningful legacy tied to the Phyllis Wheatley Association, an organization created to support Black women relocating to Los Angeles during an era marked by housing discrimination and limited access to resources. Sponsored by influential women’s groups such as the Altura Club and the Athenians, the home once served as a place of refuge, connection, and advancement, providing affordable housing, employment referrals, and community support to women building new lives in the city. Today, that powerful sense of purpose and presence still resonates throughout the property. The expansive main residence spans three stories and offers an incredible amount of living space with nine bedrooms and five bathrooms, creating endless possibilities for multigenerational living, creative use, or extended household needs. Rich with character and scale, the home blends historic significance with the energy of a property ready for its next chapter. Generous gathering spaces and the property’s unique layout create an entertainer’s dream atmosphere, ideal for hosting elegant events, celebrations, and memorable gatherings around the grand piano. The kitchen is outfitted with high-end Wolf appliances, complemented by a Wolf outdoor grill that extends the experience into the beautifully designed garden spaces. A built-in hot tub and charming greenhouse further enhance the property’s sense of retreat and relaxation, while a stunning stained glass window rising along the staircase to the second level brings warmth, artistry, and unforgettable character to the interior. Tucked behind the main residence is a fully permitted two-story ADU. Altogether, this is a rare opportunity to own a property that stands not only as a substantial residential compound, but also as an important piece of Los Angeles cultural history.

remarks: Sun, Flat Open Land, and a Full Remodel in Boulder Creek.  Two things rarely come together on a Boulder Creek property: real sunlight and flat, open, usable ground. This one has both, on nearly seven-tenths of an acre that stays level and open. Room to garden, gather, park, or simply let the light in, without a hillside dictating every decision. In redwood country, that much flat, sunny land is the hard part to find, and here it's already done. Inside, the home has been fully remodeled with high-end appliances and finishes throughout. The kitchen is finished in quartz, and the primary bath is built around double sinks and an oversized shower. Enjoy an additional space for flexible use, includes kitchen and bath. The setting still gives you the redwoods  the shade, the quiet, the trees you came up here for  while the sun reaches the ground, which is what makes the outdoor space livable across the seasons. Boulder Creek sits at the heart of the San Lorenzo Valley, its historic downtown a short stretch of Highway 9 lined with Victorian storefronts, local shops and restaurants, and the murals that trace the town back to the 1870s. The redwoods of Big Basin rise just up Highway 236. Santa Cruz and the coast are down the valley; the Silicon Valley side is over the ridge on Highway 35.
